# HERMES 2022 Overview

HERMES is the project management method of the Swiss federal administration.
It structures a project into phases, roles, and outcomes (deliverables).

## Phases

HERMES defines four phases that every traditional project passes through:
Initialisierung, Konzept, Realisierung, and Einführung. Each phase ends at a
milestone quality gate where the steering committee decides whether the project
may continue. The Initialisierung phase produces the Projektauftrag; the Konzept
phase produces the Studie and the Schutzbedarfsanalyse.

## Roles

HERMES assigns clear roles. The Auftraggeber (client) owns the business case and
sponsors the project. The Projektleiter (project manager) plans and steers daily
work. The Anwender (user) validates that outcomes meet operational needs, and the
Qualitäts- und Risikomanager safeguards quality gates and risk controls.

## Outcomes

Outcomes are the documents, states, and decisions a project must deliver. Key
mandatory outcomes include the Projektauftrag, the Studie, the
Schutzbedarfsanalyse, and the abschliessende Projektbeurteilung. A minimum set of
outcomes is mandatory for every scenario; additional outcomes are selected to fit
the project's scope and risk profile.
